## Rule established by demos

The grid has a uniform background and a contrasting foreground color (which varies between examples). Preserve every original cell. For each row and each column independently, count occurrences of the non-background foreground color. If a line has **at least three** foreground cells, paint every background cell strictly between its first and last foreground cells with color 2. Do not extend beyond those endpoints. Lines with fewer than three foreground cells are not filled. This is not limited to single-cell gaps: fill all background positions within the interval. Do not overwrite original foreground or background outside qualifying intervals.

The 3-cell threshold matters: in demo 2, rows with only two 5s at c3 and c8 were unchanged, whereas rows 8 and 12 with at least three 5s had their internal gaps filled. Demo 1 rows with several 0s had all intervening gaps filled, while the row with only two zeros remained unchanged. Demo 3 similarly fills spans between multiple 6s in each row/column.

## Verified test solution

Task test had background 1, foreground 3, and output color 2. Qualifying rows/columns were:
- Row 13 (0-indexed): 3s across c10–18 and c20–21, so fill c19 with 2.
- Rows 14, 16, and 17: each has 3s at c10, c13, and c21, so fill all background positions between c10 and c21 (preserving the c13 3).
- Row 15 has only two 3s (c10 and c21), so do not fill that row horizontally.
- Column 13 has 3s at rows 13, 14, 16, 17, and 23; fill background gaps between the endpoints, namely rows 15 and 18–22 with 2.
- Other rows/columns do not qualify or have no background gaps to fill.
